who_for.title: First-time pedal-free riders
who_for.body: Balance-first learning: no pedals, no stabilisers. Children learn to glide and steer, then move to a pedal bike with real confidence.

who_for.title: A gift that means something
who_for.body: A handmade keepsake, not a plastic shop bike — built by you, kept for years, often passed down to the next child.

who_for.title: Parents who want to build it WITH their child
who_for.body: Few parts, forgiving bamboo, no power tools. A short, joyful project you can do alongside a toddler — or as a surprise.

faq.q: What age and size is this for?
faq.a: Designed for children roughly aged 2–5, as a balance (pedal-free) first bike. The right fit depends on your child's inside-leg measurement more than age — send us their height and inside leg and we'll confirm it suits them. (FLAG: confirm exact age/height/inside-leg range and minimum age with James.)

faq.q: Is it light enough for a toddler to handle?
faq.a: Bamboo is naturally light and the balance frame is small, so it's made to be manageable for little legs. We don't want to publish a weight we haven't measured — please confirm the finished weight in kg before this goes live. (FLAG: real weight needed.)

Balance bikes teach the hard part first — balancing and steering — without pedals or stabilisers. Children glide with their feet, then move straight to a pedal bike, usually skipping stabilisers altogether.

faq.q: How hard is the build, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It's our simplest kit — fewer parts than an adult frame and around 8–12 hours, comfortably a weekend. No power tools: just basic hand tools (hacksaw, files, sandpaper, tape) and a work surface. Most builders start with zero experience, and our community can help if you get stuck.

faq.q: Is it safe and strong enough for a child?
faq.a: The bamboo frame is sealed and tough — around 28,000 PSI tensile strength (comparable to mild steel), under 1% failure across 4,000+ builds, and tested with Swansea University. As with any child's bike, fit a helmet and supervise early rides. (FLAG: confirm any child-specific safety standard or wording with James.)
